data.title: The future is not self-hosted
data.author: drew_lytle
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了亚马逊Kindle用户无法再将电子书下载到电脑上的问题，质疑用户是否真正拥有这些书籍，还是仅仅是从亚马逊“租用”它们。文章指出，数字商品一直以来都是以授权形式购买，而非真正拥有。这种情况不仅限于媒体，还包括存储在各大公司服务器上的个人数据。作者讲述了自己通过自建云服务器，摆脱大公司控制，完全拥有和掌控自己数字生活的经历。自托管（self-hosting）是指在自己的硬件上运行服务器和应用程序，虽然工作量大，但对追求控制权和自由的人来说具有吸引力。作者详细介绍了自己搭建家庭服务器的过程，并认为自托管虽不易普及，但对重视数据自主的人是一个选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自托管（self-hosting）的可行性、复杂性、隐私性以及社区协作的可能性

不同观点：
• MoreQARespect认为，自托管目前类似于iPhone出现前的手机世界。技术爱好者已经在使用这些工具，但普通用户尚未接受，因为设置过程繁琐且缺乏美观、符合人体工学的体验。一旦自托管变得无缝且易用，需求可能会迅速增长。
• stego-tech同意自托管优于企业云服务，但指出其复杂性和成本使其不适合普通用户。同时强调，隐私、安全和主权问题需要更广泛的讨论，并提出公共数据中心和基础设施的设想，呼吁开源项目简化部署流程。
• hermitcrab强调了网络应用（SAAS）的流行，但指出了订阅模式的长期成本问题，认为下载软件仍有其优势，如一次性付费和数据本地存储。
• bix6指出，许多人没有意识到他们放弃了多少隐私，并以自己为例说明通过自托管获得隐私的难度和工作量。
• jqpabc123认为，社区托管需要超越个体主义，但目前仍缺乏对系统管理员的激励机制，最终可能仍需依赖企业服务。
• singpolyma3质疑将自托管等同于在家中拥有物理服务器的观点，提出通过SSO技术实现自托管和社区协作的可能性。
• torium引用Stallman的观点，推荐不需要互联网连接的Pocketbook电子书阅读器，以避免数字内容限制。
• palata讨论了“托管托管”服务，如Hetzner或Infomaniak提供的Nextcloud实例，认为这是一种简化和安全的选择，但仍存在数据访问问题。
• hengheng不信任社区托管，担心E2E加密无法证明，以及社区共享服务器可能被没收的风险。
• dathinab建议立法强制规定数字内容购买的透明度和可用性，反对企业滥用商业行为。
• kbody提到Umbrel等项目提供了良好的用户体验，并认为更好的家庭互联网连接将使自托管更加普及。
• V__不同意一些作者的观点，认为自托管更多是关于数据和软件的控制，而非硬件的位置，并质疑社区云服务的可行性。
• mmstgshj提到disroot.org已经在提供部分E2EE服务，并明确标示哪些服务是E2EE。
• will5421询问是否可以通过VPN让朋友访问自托管服务器，提出创建共享相册的可能性。

补充讨论：
• 自托管的复杂性和用户体验是讨论的核心，许多人认为需要简化和美化以吸引更多用户。
• 社区托管和协作的可能性被多次提及，但存在信任、技术可行性和法律风险等争议。
• 数字内容的拥有权和可用性问题引发了对现行商业模式和立法的批评。
• 不同用户对隐私、安全和便利的优先级不同，导致对自托管和社区托管的看法多样化。

44682175.article_content:
Hey friends 👋,
A few months ago, Amazon announced that
Kindle users would no longer be able to download and back up their book libraries to their computers
. Thankfully, I still have access to my library because I saw
this video
by Jared Henderson warning of the change and downloaded all ~400 of my books immediately.
But for those that didn't, the only way for them to view the books they own is through a Kindle or the Kindle app.
Which raises the question: do they even own those books?
If you can only access an item through an intermediary that decides the terms and means of your access, I'd say
no
. You don't own your books on Kindle. You rent them from Amazon.
And Amazon agrees with this. When they closed this direct way for users to access their eBooks, they also updated the language in the Kindle store to say
users are purchasing
licenses
– not books!
Now, this isn't new. Companies like Amazon have been playing dirty with Digital Rights Management (DRM) since the Internet's inception. Purchased digital goods have always been licenses more than owned assets.
What's changed is they're bold enough now to say the quiet part out loud: that we own nothing.
But this situation extends beyond the realms of media. Even your own data: your documents in Dropbox or Google Drive, your photos in iCloud or Google Photos, your emails, chat history,
everything
is rented space on these large corporations computers.
And at any point, they can choose to change the terms and conditions of that rental agreement. They can (and I'm sure they do) train AI models on all of your content. They can (and do) change the pricing tiers for their plans to upsell you. They can (and do) make it
extremely difficult
to migrate to different services.
In our techno-feudalistic dystopia, they're the landlords. We're the serfs.
But over the past few weeks – with the help of a growing group of rebels fighting to take back ownership and control over their digital lives – I did something radical: I built my own cloud.
My wife and I now have a computer in our house that runs open-source equivalents to Google Drive, Google Photos, Audible, Kindle, and Netflix. It syncs to all of our devices. It's secured behind our own VPN. And it's wholly, truly owned by us.
And this week, I want to share with you how I did it, what I learned, and why I think self-hosting is NOT the future we should be fighting for.
Let's start by answering the simple question...
What is self-hosting?
To explain what self-hosting is, I find it helpful to demystify what we mean when we talk about "the cloud". Cloud-hosted apps like Drive and Google Photos are simply applications running on computers that we access through the internet.
Those computers are colloquially called
servers
. They're usually racked together in large datacenters and programmed to coordinate with computers across the world to distribute workloads and process requests from users as quickly as possible with minimal downtime.
These computers also handle finding, storing, and backing up the data you upload to these apps.
The cloud is a very smart, complicated, interconnected network of computers. That's why engineers and system administrators
love
when people use this far more reductive but sufficient definition of it:
The cloud is just someone else's computer.
Self
-hosting is when you have a computer in your house do those same things, but on a much smaller scale. You maintain the hardware. You set up the servers. You manage the applications. You store and backup your data. You troubleshoot issues when things (inevitably) go wrong.
If that sounds like a lot of work,
it is
. For this reason alone, self-hosting is impractical for most people. There's a reason Jeff Geerling – one of the many online self-hosting gurus – sells a shirt that says,
"Cosplaying as a sys admin"
.
But if you
really
value control, freedom and flexibility – or you're a software engineer that suffers from mild mania and hyperfixation – it can be a pretty fun time.
So, what's on my home server?
Before I talk about the services I'm using to backup photos, store files, and stream movies, let me quickly run you through the setup process.
Deep breath.
After watching
this video
by Hardware Haven, I bought a
Lenovo P520
off eBay with a 3.70 GHz Intel Xeon W-2135 and 128GB of RAM.
When it arrived, I installed a GTX 1660Ti graphics card with 6 GB of vRAM, flashed a 500 GB SSD with Proxmox, set up four 8 TB HDDs in a MergerFS pool with Snapraid for parity, and added a 2 TB NVMe SSD to use as a storage cache.
After that, I installed Tailscale and created a fresh Ubuntu LXC. Then, I installed Tailscale and Docker on the virtual machine, pulled down a GitHub repo containing all of my setup scripts and
compose.yml
files, hacked into the mainframe, and ran
docker compose up -d
.
Gasp.
I understand that to some (maybe most) of you, those words meant nothing. That's kind of the point. All of that took 138 words to describe but took me the better part of two w

data.author: simonpure
data.article_summary: Efrit 是一个集成于 Emacs 的 AI 编码助手，通过原生 Elisp 评估实现高级自动化。它提供多种界面：efrit-chat 用于多轮对话，efrit-do 用于自然语言命令执行，efrit 用于结构化交互，efrit-agent-run 用于多步骤自动化。Efrit 支持直接 Elisp 评估、多轮对话、工具集成、安全设计和深色主题。安装需要 Emacs 28.1 及以上版本和 Anthropic API Key。使用命令包括 M-x efrit-chat、M-x efrit-do 等，支持自定义配置和快捷键绑定。Efrit 强调 Elisp 中心化，提供灵活的配置和调试选项。

Efrit - AI-Powered Emacs Coding Assistant
A sophisticated AI coding agent that leverages Emacs' native programmability through direct Elisp evaluation.
Overview
Efrit is a conversational AI assistant that integrates seamlessly with Emacs, providing multiple interfaces for different types of tasks:
efrit-chat
- Multi-turn conversational interface for complex discussions and code development
efrit-do
- Natural language command execution for quick tasks
efrit
- Command interface for structured interactions
efrit-agent-run
- Advanced agent loop for multi-step automation
Key Features
Direct Elisp Evaluation
: Leverages Emacs' native programmability without complex abstractions
Multi-turn Conversations
: Maintains context across multiple exchanges with configurable turn limits
Tool Integration
: Can execute Emacs functions, manipulate buffers, and interact with the environment
Safety-First Design
: Confirmation systems and comprehensive error handling
Dark Theme Friendly
: Adaptive colors that work with any Emacs theme
Installation
Prerequisites
Emacs
: Version 28.1 or later
Anthropic API Key
: Get yours from
Anthropic Console
Internet Connection
: Required for Claude API access
Quick Installation
Clone the repository
:
git clone https://github.com/steveyegge/efrit.git
cd
efrit
Add to your Emacs configuration
(
~/.emacs.d/init.el
):
(
add-to-list
'load-path
"
/path/to/efrit
"
)
(
require
'efrit
)
Configure your API key
in
~/.authinfo
:
machine api.anthropic.com login personal password YOUR_API_KEY_HERE
Restart Emacs
and test with
M-x efrit-chat
Alternative Installation Methods
Emergency Emacs Setup

data.title: Grindr Won't Let Users Say 'No Zionists'
data.author: malfmalf
data.article_summary: Grindr禁止用户在个人资料中添加“no Zionists”字样，尽管其他关于政治和宗教偏好的表述是被允许的。一些用户在尝试加入该短语时收到错误提示，而类似“no Arabs”、“no Muslims”等其他表述则未被限制。该规则未在服务条款中明确说明。此前，Grindr曾因种族歧视问题移除种族过滤器，但执行过程滞后。有报道称，亲以色列的用户曾抱怨在约会应用上遭遇敌意。批评者认为，平台未能有效保护少数群体免受压迫。Grindr尚未对此作出回应。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：平台对特定词汇的限制

不同观点：
• [malfmalf] 认为平台在用户个人简介中限制了特定词汇如 "no zionist, no zionists" 的使用，但允许其他政治和宗教相关的表述。这引发对其审查标准和公平性的质疑。
   
• [orphea] 对限制的技术实现感到好奇，提出是否可以通过改变词汇形式（如替换字母、使用不同字符）来绕过限制。这表明对平台审查机制的实现细节感兴趣，并暗示可能存在规避手段。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于平台对某些特定词汇的限制是否合理，以及这些限制是否存在双重标准。
- [orphea] 的评论还暗示了对审查机制有效性的潜在挑战，即用户可能会尝试通过技术手段绕过此类限制。
- 未明确讨论的是平台设置此类限制的具体原因或背景，这可能涉及平台政策、政治敏感性或外部压力。

Grindr Won’t Let Users Say 'No Zionists'
Samantha Cole
·
Jul 24, 2025
at 12:35 PM
An error message appears saying "The following are not allowed: no zionist, no zionists" when users try to add the phrase to their bios, but any number of other phrases about political and religious preferences are allowed.
The error message and the Grindr logo. Collage via 404 Media
Grindr won’t allow users to add “no Zionists” to their profiles, but allows any number of other phrases that state political, religious, and ethnic preferences, according to 404 Media’s tests of the platform and user reports.
Several users received an error message that says “The following are not allowed: no zionist, no zionists,” when they tried to add the phrases to their bios on Thursday. I tested this myself on a new Grindr account, and received the same error message. I was able to add “Zionist” to my profile (without “no”), however, and could also add any phrase I could think of: “no Arabs,” “no Blacks,” “no Palestinians,” “no Muslims,” “no Christians,” “no Jews,” “no trans,” “no Republicans,” “no Democrats,” and so on. “No Zionist[s]” was the only phrase that was blocked in my testing.
Others have seen this message
as early as May 2024
. It’s not clear when Grindr started implementing this rule; “no Zionists” doesn’t appear anywhere in its
terms of service.
Screenshot from Grindr showing "the following is not allowed: no zionist, no zionists" error
Its terms of service does state, however: “You will NOT post, store, send, transmit, or disseminate any information or material which a reasonable person could deem to be objectionable, defamatory, libelous, offensive, obscene, indecent, pornographic, harassing, threatening, embarrassing, distressing, vulgar, hateful, racially or ethnically or otherwise offensive to any group or individual, intentionally misleading, false, or otherwise inappropriate, regardless of whether this material or its dissemination is unlawful.”
In 2020, Grindr removed its ethnicity filter, writing in its
announcement
: “We will continue to fight racism on Grindr, both through dialogue with our community and a zero-tolerance policy for racism and hate speech on our platform. As part of this commitment, and based on your feedback, we have decided to remove the ethnicity filter from our next release.⁣” But the BBC and other outlets noticed
that the app didn’t actually remove it
for weeks and several updates after the announcement.
Grindr founder
Joel Simkhai is Israeli
and
left the company in 2018
after it was sold to a Chinese gaming company. In September 2024, The Forward reported that “pro-Israel Jews” complained that they felt like they
faced hostility on dating apps
for displaying Israeli flag emojis or identifying as Zionist. In March 2025, the Association for LGBTQ Equality in Israel, known as the Aguda, reported “a significant uptick in attempted lynchings and stabbings that used the popular dating app Grindr to target LGBT people in the North,” the
Jerusalem Post reported
, where attackers allegedly created fake Grindr profiles to lure victims to them.
“It seems pretty explicitly pro-colonization and protecting of the ideology that genocide and ethnic cleansing are okay for certain groups to perform as long as it upholds your own personal or capitalistic interests,” Green, a Grindr user I spoke to who also saw this error message, told me. “It’s gross. And to put energy towards protecting a blatantly bigoted ideology and not put the same energy towards protecting minority groups is pathetic. So fuck Grindr and its inability to intersect queer oppression with the oppression of other groups.”
Grindr did not immediately respond to 404 Media’s request for comment.
About the author
Sam Cole is writing from the far reaches of the internet, about sexuality, the adult industry, online culture, and AI. She's the author of How Sex Changed the Internet and the Internet Changed Sex.

data.title: Vet is a safety net for the curl | bash pattern
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: "vet" 是一个命令行工具，旨在解决常见的 `curl | bash` 不安全执行模式。它提供了一个安全的工作流，允许用户在执行远程脚本前进行检查、比对历史版本、进行语法分析，并明确要求用户批准执行，从而提高远程代码执行的安全性和透明度。用户可以通过 Homebrew 或手动下载并审查安装脚本来安装 "vet"。该工具还提供了非交互模式和多种选项以适应不同使用场景。其设计哲学强调安全性，依赖 Bash 4+ 的现代功能以确保稳健性和可读性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 `curl|bash` 安装方式的安全性、可靠性及其实际应用的讨论

不同观点：
• **反对 `curl|bash` 的方式**：[pxeger1] 认为 `curl|bash` 的问题不在于脚本是否恶意，而在于脚本可能写得不专业或未考虑用户需求，导致安装过程脆弱或不符合标准。他更倾向于手动下载和安装二进制文件以确保稳定性。

• **使用工具审查脚本**：[networked] 建议使用 `vipe`（来自 moreutils）在执行脚本前先在编辑器中查看和修改，从而增加安全性。不过，他也提到 `vipe` 默认不会运行脚本，需要手动处理。

• **检测服务器端攻击**：[jjgreen] 提到 `curl|bash` 模式可以被服务器检测到，可能导致针对性攻击。他质疑即使审查了脚本，后续依然需要信任软件仓库的安全性。

• **历史对比与反恶意软件措施**：[baq] 将 `curl|bash` 与过去的 Windows 下载安装方式对比，认为反恶意软件（如杀毒软件）是解决方案，并指出当前流行的 `npm` 和 `docker` 安装方式同样存在风险。

• **执行环境隔离**：[totetsu] 建议使用 `firejail` 或 `bubblewrap` 等工具在执行脚本前查看其具体操作，避免潜在风险。

• **简化安装的必要性**：[Galanwe] 强调 `curl|bash` 是为了跳过依赖包管理器进行安装，而引入额外的工具可能违背这一初衷。

• **复杂安装链的隐患**：[mid-kid] 指出许多 `curl` 脚本只是引导脚本，可能触发一系列下载和安装操作，用户难以验证整个过程的完整性和安全性，建议通过包管理器或手动安装来避免潜在问题。

• **操作系统对实验性的限制**：[jrm4] 认为现代操作系统（如 Windows 和 macOS）限制了用户的实验性操作，使得安全与自由的平衡难以实现。

• **包管理器的优势**：[aezart] 强调使用 `deb` 等包管理器安装软件的优势，包括处理依赖、安装路径和系统整合性等问题，认为这能增强用户对软件的信心。

• **寻找最佳 Linux 发行版**：[sgc] 提出寻找一个在包管理、配置文件位置、软件更新、安全性及自定义灵活性上表现较好的 Linux 发行版的问题，并对自己使用的 Debian/Ubuntu 提出了一些不满。

• **增加域名验证**：[Sanzig] 建议通过 DNS 记录中的公钥对脚本进行签名验证，以防止服务器被劫持后的攻击。

• **审计与依赖管理工具**：[burnt-resistor] 强调使用如 `equivs` 和 `cruft-ng` 等工具进行依赖管理和系统变更审计，认为这些是更好的实践方式。

• **容器化执行脚本**：[tyingq] 建议在无根容器中运行脚本，并通过文件系统差异分析和审计事件来评估脚本的影响，认为容器隔离能提供一定程度的保护。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中反复提到 `curl|bash` 模式的安全隐患，特别是脚本的不可预见性和潜在的系统破坏性。
• 一些用户建议通过脚本审查、签名验证、容器隔离等技术手段来增强安全性。
• 包管理器和手动安装被认为是更可靠的选择，但也存在对操作系统依赖管理和自定义灵活性的讨论。
• 有用户提到现代操作系统对用户实验性操作的限制，并对比了过去和现在的软件安装方式。

vet
is a command-line tool that acts as a safety net for the common but risky
curl | bash
pattern. It lets you inspect remote scripts for changes, run them through a linter, and require your explicit approval before they can execute.
Don't just run it,
vet
it.
The Problem
We've all seen this pattern for installing software:
#
This is convenient, but you're blindly trusting the remote script.
curl -sSL https://example.com/install.sh
|
bash
This is dangerous. The script could be malicious, the server could be compromised, or a transient network error could result in executing a partial script.
The Solution: vet
vet
wraps this process in a secure, interactive workflow:
Fetch:
It downloads the remote script to a temporary location.
Diff & Review:
It shows you what, if anything, has changed since the last time you ran this script.
Lint:
If you have shellcheck installed, it automatically analyzes the script for potential bugs or malicious patterns.
Confirm:
It prompts you for explicit approval before executing anything.
#
The new, safer way.
vet https://example.com/install.sh
Installation
We believe you should never blindly trust a script from the internet—not even ours. That's why
vet
exists. The installation process itself is a perfect demonstration of the problem
vet
solves.
Homebrew (macOS/Linux) - Recommended
The easiest and recommended way to install
vet
is via Homebrew.
# First, tap the official repository
brew tap vet-run/vet
# Now, install the formula
brew install vet-run
Note:
The formula is named
vet-run
to avoid a conflict with another tool in the Homebrew ecosystem, but this command will correctly install the
vet
executable on your system.
Manual Installation
The Safe Way
If you don't use Homebrew, or if you simply wish to follow the security-first principle that
vet
champions, you can perform a manual installation. This is the two-step "Download, then Review" process that demonstrates exactly what
vet
automates for you.
Download the installer
:
Choose one of the following sources. The first is the official project domain, and the second is a direct link to the GitHub release asset.
Option A: Official project domain
curl -o install_vet.sh https://getvet.sh/install.sh
Option B: Direct GitHub Release Link
curl -L -o install_vet.sh https://github.com/vet-run/vet/releases/latest/download/install.sh
Review the installer's code.
Open it in a text editor or use less to ensure it's not doing anything suspicious. It's a simple script that downloads the correct vet script and moves it to /usr/local/bin.
less install_vet.sh
Run the installer you just vetted:
bash install_vet.sh
Congratulations! You just manually performed the process that vet will now automate for you.
The "Trusting" One-Liner (The Anti-Pattern)
#
This is the curl-to-bash pattern.
#
Don't actually do this. That's the whole point.
curl -sL https://getvet.sh/install.sh
|
bash
Usage
#
Basic usage
vet
<
URL
>
#
Example with a real-world installer
vet https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.1/install.sh
#
Pass arguments to the remote script
#
All arguments after the URL are passed directly to the script.
vet https://example.com/setup.sh --user myuser --version latest
#
Non-interactive mode for trusted scripts in automated environments (e.g., CI/CD)
vet --force https://my-trusted-internal-script.sh
Options
-f, --force
Skip all interactive prompts and execute immediately. Use with caution.
-h, --help
Display the help message.
Project Philosophy & Technical Decisions
Bash 4+ is a Required Dependency
vet
is intentionally written to leverage modern bash features (arrays, [[ ... ]], pipefail). We believe that for a security-focused tool, sacrificing robustness and readability for POSIX sh compatibility would be a dangerous trade-off.
The safety features provided by modern bash are non-negotiable for
vet
's mission.

• **复杂安装链的隐患**：[mid-kid] 指出许多 `curl` 脚本只是引导脚本，可能触发一系列下载和安装操作，用户难以验证整个过程的完整性和安全性，建议通过包管理器或手动安装来避免潜在问题。

• **操作系统对实验性的限制**：[jrm4] 认为现代操作系统（如 Windows 和 macOS）限制了用户的实验性操作，使得安全与自由的平衡难以实现。

• **包管理器的优势**：[aezart] 强调使用 `deb` 等包管理器安装软件的优势，包括处理依赖、安装路径和系统整合性等问题，认为这能增强用户对软件的信心。

• **寻找最佳 Linux 发行版**：[sgc] 提出寻找一个在包管理、配置文件位置、软件更新、安全性及自定义灵活性上表现较好的 Linux 发行版的问题，并对自己使用的 Debian/Ubuntu 提出了一些不满。

• **增加域名验证**：[Sanzig] 建议通过 DNS 记录中的公钥对脚本进行签名验证，以防止服务器被劫持后的攻击。

• **审计与依赖管理工具**：[burnt-resistor] 强调使用如 `equivs` 和 `cruft-ng` 等工具进行依赖管理和系统变更审计，认为这些是更好的实践方式。

• **容器化执行脚本**：[tyingq] 建议在无根容器中运行脚本，并通过文件系统差异分析和审计事件来评估脚本的影响，认为容器隔离能提供一定程度的保护。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中反复提到 `curl|bash` 模式的安全隐患，特别是脚本的不可预见性和潜在的系统破坏性。
• 一些用户建议通过脚本审查、签名验证、容器隔离等技术手段来增强安全性。
• 包管理器和手动安装被认为是更可靠的选择，但也存在对操作系统依赖管理和自定义灵活性的讨论。
• 有用户提到现代操作系统对用户实验性操作的限制，并对比了过去和现在的软件安装方式。

data.title: Detekt – A static code analyzer for Kotlin
data.author: TheWiggles
data.article_summary: detekt 是一个帮助开发者编写更整洁 Kotlin 代码的工具，让开发者可以专注于构建出色的软件。它易于集成，支持 Gradle、Maven、Bazel 等多种构建系统，适用于 Android、JVM、JS、Native 和多平台项目。detekt 还支持通过自定义规则轻松扩展，以发现和修复代码中的不良模式。作为一个开源项目，它由社区驱动，用户可以在 GitHub 上参与贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kotlin在后端开发中的使用及其相关工具的支持情况

不同观点：
• smokel：对Kotlin在后端开发中的使用表示好奇，并提到尽管Kotlin在语法和功能上有优势（如扩展方法、更好的null检查），但Java正在迎头赶上。他还指出，Kotlin可能带来的供应商锁定风险让一些资深同事不愿转向Kotlin。

• jascha_eng：指出Kotlin的一个主要问题是与IntelliJ的锁定，因为VSCode对Kotlin的支持非常差，这影响了使用现代AI工具（如cursor）的体验。

• robch：分享了他多年使用detekt工具的经验，认为detekt是Kotlin最好的linter，特别是它能够编写利用类型解析的高级lint规则，并希望detekt能尽快支持K2编译器。

• LennyWhiteJr：对detekt给予高度评价，认为它特别适合用于强制执行项目约定，而这些约定是标准linter无法覆盖的。他还提到，借助LLM（大型语言模型），可以大幅减少创建新分析器的工作量。

• synesso：对detekt突然成为Hacker News上的热门文章表示不解，因为该工具已经存在多年。

补充讨论：
• Kotlin的供应商锁定问题：jascha_eng指出的Intellij锁定问题和smokel提到的风险相呼应，显示出这在开发者中是一个实际的顾虑。
• detekt工具的实用性：robch和LennyWhiteJr都对detekt的功能和灵活性表示赞赏，特别是它对自定义规则的支持和与现代AI工具的结合。
• 对热门话题的疑惑：synesso对detekt成为热门讨论话题表示不解，表明该工具虽然实用，但其突然受到关注可能令人意外。

争议焦点：
• Kotlin相对于Java的优势是否足以抵消其潜在的锁定风险。

data.title: You can run Doom and other graphical apps in Android's Linux Terminal
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 在最新的Android Canary版本中，Linux终端应用现在支持运行图形化Linux应用程序，这是该功能的一个重大进展。通过新增的“Display”按钮，用户可以启动图形环境，运行原本无法在Android上使用的桌面应用。该终端应用允许启动Debian虚拟机，支持完整Linux应用，而此次更新还加入了硬件加速选项，为运行更强大的Linux软件和游戏铺平了道路。尽管目前该功能仅在Canary版本中提供，尚未进入Beta或稳定版，但它标志着Google在整合Chrome OS和Android的进程中迈出了重要一步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Minecraft Java Edition 是否应在手机上运行以及相关潜在问题

不同观点：
• **支持在手机上运行Minecraft Java Edition**：xeonmc认为，能够在手机上玩Minecraft Java Edition是一个重要的功能，暗示该功能会受到用户的欢迎和追捧。这一观点强调了跨平台体验的吸引力，尤其是对于希望在移动设备上享受完整游戏体验的玩家。

• **对潜在问题的担忧**：Bluestein的观点则侧重于可能伴随该功能而来的问题，特别是涉及第三方干预和支付处理的限制。Bluestein指出，如果某些内容引起争议（例如涉及成人内容或敏感内容），第三方可能会介入干预，甚至支付处理方也可能因此放弃对该服务的支持。这表明了对技术或内容监管问题的潜在担忧。

补充讨论：
• **功能吸引力与现实限制的张力**：xeonmc关注功能的创新性和用户需求的满足，而Bluestein则更关心这一功能实现后面临的外部限制和潜在风险。两者之间的讨论体现了技术创新和现实监管之间的张力。

Mobile
You can finally run Doom and other graphical apps in Android's Linux Terminal
The Terminal app can now run full graphical Linux apps in the latest Android Canary build
By
Mishaal Rahman
•
17 hours ago
•
0
•
Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority
TL;DR
Android’s Linux Terminal app can now run graphical Linux apps in the latest Canary build, a major step forward for the feature.
A new “Display” button launches a graphical environment, letting users run full desktop apps that aren’t available on Android.
Hardware acceleration can also be enabled for better performance, paving the way for running even more powerful Linux software and games.
The
Linux Terminal app
that Google introduced earlier this year is one of the most exciting new features in Android, not for what it currently does but for what it can potentially do. The Terminal app lets you boot up an instance of Debian in a virtual machine, allowing you to run full-fledged Linux apps that aren’t available on Android. Unfortunately, the current version of the Terminal app is limited to running command line programs, but that’s set to change in the near future. In the new
Android Canary
build that Google released today, the Terminal app now lets you run graphical Linux apps.
Earlier this year, we ran a Linux port of
Doom in Android’s Terminal app
to showcase the app’s upcoming graphical capabilities. For months, Google has been working to add hardware acceleration support and a full graphical environment to the Linux Terminal, but the company never pushed these features to any public builds, requiring us to compile Android from source to try them out.
After installing the July 2025 Android Canary build, however, we noticed that the Terminal app has been updated with graphical app support. When you open up the Terminal app in this build, you’ll see a new button in the top right corner. This button launches the “Display” activity of the Terminal app, which forwards graphical output from the Linux VM to the Android host.
Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority
Once on this screen, you can type the ‘weston’ command to open up a graphical environment. Weston is a reference implementation of a Wayland compositor, a modern display server protocol, and it comes preinstalled with Android’s Linux Terminal.
In the graphical environment, we were able to launch apps like Gedit, a basic text editor. We didn’t try running Doom again, but you can see what that looks like in the video we recorded earlier this year.
By default, hardware acceleration isn’t enabled in the Linux Terminal. To enable it, you need to create an empty file named ‘
virglrenderer
’ and place it in the ‘
/sdcard/linux
’ directory. If you see a toast message that reads “VirGL enabled” when you open the Linux Terminal, then you’ve done things correctly.
The addition of graphical app support in the Linux Terminal is a big deal, as it opens the door to running many useful Linux programs that aren’t available on Android. It also opens the door to running PC games in the future, though more work will need to be done to make them compatible, especially since most Android devices have ARM CPUs. Regardless, this is a big step forward in Google’s plans to
combine Chrome OS and Android
into a single platform, so we’re excited to see how things proceed.
Although this feature is enabled in the latest Android Canary build, we don’t know when it’ll land in the Beta or Stable channels. We’re hoping that Google will roll it out in the second quarterly release of
Android 16
, which is scheduled to roll out in December. However, there’s no guarantee the company will do so.

data.title: Microsoft admits it 'cannot guarantee' data sovereignty
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 微软在法国参议院作证时承认，根据《云法案》，如果特朗普政府要求获取存储在微软服务器的欧洲客户数据，公司无法保证数据主权。微软法国公共与法律事务总监Anton Carniaux表示，虽然公司会尽力抵制无根据的数据请求，并在可能时通知客户，但若请求合法，微软仍可能被迫交出数据。尽管微软尚未收到美国政府对欧洲数据的索取要求，且公司已采取措施尽量将数据保留在欧盟内，但仍无法完全保证数据不被转移至美国。这一问题引发了欧洲对数据主权和国家安全的担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧盟国家政府在技术合同中的支出以及对数据隐私的担忧

不同观点：
• oriettaxx 认为，欧盟各国的民族主义政治家对意大利公共部门向微软支付巨额费用（过去三年达20亿欧元）保持沉默是可笑且可悲的。这暗示了对公共资金流向跨国公司以及可能带来的数据隐私风险的担忧。

• duxup 则指出，任何在一个国家运营的公司都可能被当地政府或法院要求提供数据，因此质疑是否真的有公司能够保证不交出数据。这不是对微软或现行政府政策的辩护，而是对公司是否能真正保护用户数据隐私的普遍性怀疑。

补充讨论：
• oriettaxx 的评论隐含了对政府在技术采购中缺乏透明度和问责制的批评，特别是涉及跨国公司如微软时。

• duxup 的观点强调了在全球化背景下，数据隐私保护的复杂性，并指出了政府要求公司提供数据这一普遍存在的法律风险。

• 争议的焦点在于：公共资金的大量支出是否合理，以及跨国公司在面对政府数据请求时能否有效保护用户隐私。这些讨论反映了公众对政府行为和公司责任的双重质疑。

Microsoft admits it 'cannot guarantee' data sovereignty
11
Under oath in French Senate, exec says it would be compelled – however unlikely – to pass local customer info to US admin
Paul Kunert
Fri 25 Jul 2025
//
13:00 UTC
Microsoft says it "cannot guarantee" data sovereignty to customers in France – and by implication the wider European Union – should the Trump administration demand access to customer information held on its servers.
The
Cloud Act
is a law that gives the US government authority to obtain digital data held by US-based tech corporations irrespective of whether that data is stored on servers at home or on foreign soil. It is said to compel these companies, via warrant or subpoena, to accept the request.
Talking on
June 18
before a Senate inquiry into public procurement and the role it plays in European digital sovereignty, Microsoft France's Anton Carniaux, director of public and legal affairs, along with Pierre Lagarde, technical director of the public sector, were quizzed by local politicians.
Asked of any technical or legal mechanisms that could prevent this access under the Cloud Act, Carniaux said it had "contractually committed to our clients, including those in the public sector, to resist these requests when they are unfounded."
"We have implemented a very rigorous system, initiated during the Obama era by legal actions against requests from the authorities, which allows us to obtain concessions from the American government. We begin by analyzing very precisely the validity of a request and reject it if it is unfounded."
He said that Microsoft asks the US administration to redirect it to the client.
"When this proves impossible, we respond in extremely specific and limited cases. I would like to point out that the government cannot make requests that are not precisely defined."
Carniaux added: "If we must communicate, we ask to be able to notify the client concerned." He said that under the former Obama administration, Microsoft took cases to the US Supreme Court and as such ensured requests are "more focused, precise, justified and legally sound."
The Cloud Act was signed into law in 2018 following challenges the FBI faced when getting data via service providers through Store Communications Act warrants, which was itself legislated before cloud computing became a viable thing. Microsoft challenged previous requests, including one concerning a 2016 drug trafficking probe, when emails of a US citizen were held on Microsoft servers in Ireland, and
Microsoft argued
the SCA did not cover data held outside the US.
The bill was supported at the time it became law by AWS, Microsoft, and Google – and was criticized by civil rights groups. European cloud providers with skin in the game have talked up the potential data sovereignty issue for customers in the EU, although, as Microsoft has said, it has not received data requests from the US government for data held on Microsoft servers in Europe.
Back at the hearing in France, Microsoft was asked if a data request was well framed, would the corporation be "obliged to transmit the data?"
Carniaux admitted: "Absolutely, by respecting this process. But again, this has not affected any European company, or a public sector body, since we have been publishing these transparency reports."
Microsoft transparency reports are twice yearly publications in which the business reveals how it manages user data requests, content removal, and more.
Legrande chimed in to say that for the past three years Microsoft has implemented a technical environment to minimize data transfers and keep customers data within the EU, "whether at rest, in transit or being processed, or whether it is data generated by application logs, including the support part."
As proceedings continued, Carniaux was asked if in the event of an injunction that was legally justified, could he, as Microsoft director of public and legal affairs, "guarantee our committee, under oath" that data on French citizens could not be transmitted to the American government without the explicit agreement of the French government.
"No," said Carniaux, "I cannot guarantee that, but, again, it has never happened before."
The Register
asked Microsoft to comment on this but it declined to do so.
Mark Boost, CEO at Civo, claimed: "One line of testimony just confirmed that the US hyperscaler providers cannot guarantee data sovereignty in Europe."
"Microsoft has openly admitted what many have long known: under laws like the CLOUD Act, US authorities can compel access to data held by American cloud providers, regardless of where that data physically resides. UK or EU servers make no difference when jurisdiction lies elsewhere and local subsidiaries or 'trusted' partnerships don't change that reality.

• oriettaxx 认为，欧盟各国的民族主义政治家对意大利公共部门向微软支付巨额费用（过去三年达20亿欧元）保持沉默是可笑且可悲的。这暗示了对公共资金流向跨国公司以及可能带来的数据隐私风险的担忧。

• duxup 则指出，任何在一个国家运营的公司都可能被当地政府或法院要求提供数据，因此质疑是否真的有公司能够保证不交出数据。这不是对微软或现行政府政策的辩护，而是对公司是否能真正保护用户数据隐私的普遍性怀疑。

补充讨论：
• oriettaxx 的评论隐含了对政府在技术采购中缺乏透明度和问责制的批评，特别是涉及跨国公司如微软时。

• duxup 的观点强调了在全球化背景下，数据隐私保护的复杂性，并指出了政府要求公司提供数据这一普遍存在的法律风险。

• 争议的焦点在于：公共资金的大量支出是否合理，以及跨国公司在面对政府数据请求时能否有效保护用户隐私。这些讨论反映了公众对政府行为和公司责任的双重质疑。

data.title: Checklists are hard, but still a good thing
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 文章主要内容是博客"Wandering Thoughts"及其所属的CSpace平台为了应对2025年初大量使用旧版浏览器（尤其是Chrome）爬取数据的高流量爬虫，采取了拦截措施。由于这些爬虫常使用旧版Chrome的用户代理字符串，导致一些正常用户被误拦。如果用户确实使用的是最新浏览器而被误拦，可以联系作者。此外，文章特别提到archive.*（如archive.today, archive.ph）等网站因使用类似恶意爬虫的方式存档页面也被拦截，建议使用更为规范的archive.org进行存档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： checklists在各行业中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **ww520** 认为，在业务流程自动化前，应先手动执行并创建检查清单，以明确步骤和痛点。清单在手动执行过程中完善后，自动化会更简单。
• **dvt** 强调检查清单在多个行业中未被充分使用，特别是在高风险行业如航空、军事中效果显著。然而，推广检查清单不仅需要销售软件，还需说服管理层进行运营变革，特别是在非高风险行业中，推广可能面临较大阻力。
• **blakehaswell** 区分了两种清单类型："read, do" 和 "do, confirm"。前者适用于不常使用的程序，后者则依赖记忆完成任务后确认步骤，适合常规操作且负担小。
• **kqr** 指出，许多人将检查清单与待办事项列表混淆。检查清单是标准程序，而待办事项列表是临时任务的集合，二者目的不同。
• **0xCE0** 认为检查清单是避免灾难和失败的强大工具，尤其在软件开发中，通过用户界面实现关键步骤的可视化，有助于达成共同理解。
• **regnull** 实践了创建高级检查清单应用的设想，并发布了一个共享和执行清单的平台，寻求反馈以改进。
• **rapfaria** 提出，类似编程和烹饪，检查清单和算法难以做到完全详尽，需要通过反复实践和调整来找到适合的标准。
• **squeedles** 以Ansible为例，指出自动化工具通过描述“已知良好”状态并运行清单来确保系统处于该状态，从而记录和评估清单。
• **cadamsdotcom** 建议逐步自动化检查清单，从简单步骤开始，逐步分解和自动化更复杂的步骤，通过迭代改进。
• **gleb** 认为编写有效的检查清单非常困难，需要编程和文案技能的结合，确保清单被实际使用和持续改进更具挑战性。
• **hermitcrab** 强调检查清单应是易于更新和版本控制的活文档，个人使用MyLifeOrganized并存储在Subversion中管理。
• **azmarks** 推荐Atul Gawande的《The Checklist Manifesto》一书，认为其为理解和应用检查清单提供了重要参考。
• **zhaohan_dong** 作为飞行员使用检查清单，但在软件工程中推广困难，因为软件行业的决策可逆性高且规范变化频繁。
• **susiecambria** 引用了Atul Gawande在医学领域的工作，强调检查清单在复杂领域如医疗中的重要性，并提到其推广和采纳的挑战。

补充讨论：
• 检查清单在不同行业中的应用差异，特别是在高风险与低风险行业中的价值。
• 检查清单的类型区分（"read, do" 与 "do, confirm"）以及其适用场景。
• 编写和推广有效检查清单的实际困难，特别是在非强制性行业中。
• 检查清单的逐步自动化和迭代改进策略。
• 推荐相关书籍和资源以深入理解检查清单的应用，如《The Checklist Manifesto》。

44626359.article_content:
You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

data.title: Diet, not lack of exercise, drives obesity, a new study finds
data.author: andsoitis
data.article_summary: 一项新研究发现，肥胖的主要驱动因素是饮食，而非缺乏运动。研究比较了来自34个国家和不同文化背景的人群的每日卡路里消耗，结果显示，尽管生活方式和活动水平差异很大，但他们的每日总卡路里消耗非常相似。这表明，现代社会中体重增加和肥胖的主要原因并非身体活动减少，而是饮食问题。研究人员指出，超加工食品等不健康饮食是导致肥胖的关键因素，而单纯通过增加运动量无法抵消不良饮食的影响。这项研究挑战了以往认为缺乏运动是肥胖主因的观念，强调了饮食在控制体重方面的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：饮食、运动与肥胖之间的关系，以及研究结果的解读和个人经验的分享。

不同观点：
• speby认为现代社会食物丰富、获取方便，导致人们容易不经思考地摄入过多热量，从而导致肥胖问题，特别是在美国。
• Delphiza指出评论标题具有煽动性，并不准确代表研究的结论。研究主要比较了不同经济群体之间的能量消耗，发现能量消耗的差异并不能解释肥胖的差异，因此饮食摄入可能是主要因素。研究不适用于个人健康建议。
• tonymet强调对于大多数人来说，通过运动消耗的热量有限，如一小时的中等强度跑步只能消耗1-2块饼干的热量。因此，保持或减轻体重的关键在于控制饮食，而不是依赖运动。
• bko认为人体会根据食物摄入量调整新陈代谢，适度的波动对健康有益。极端的饮食和运动习惯会导致体重问题，但适度的“冲击”可能对身体有好处。
• SeanAnderson简明扼要地指出，理论上通过饮食管理体重、通过运动管理健康是简单而有效的，但在实践中执行起来很困难。
• com2kid基于个人经验认为，在一定程度上可以通过大量运动抵消不良饮食的影响，但这种方法需要投入的运动量超出了大多数人的意愿。
• ozgrakkurt提出将包装食品公司视为对手的心理策略，帮助自己抵制不健康食品，并强调水果比包装食品更便宜。
• post_break分享了通过控制饮食和步行成功减重40磅的经验，认为不摄入脂肪比通过运动消耗脂肪更有效。
• benabbott推荐通过举重增加肌肉质量，从而提高静息代谢率，认为这是比每天进行有氧运动更有效的长期策略。
• RobKohr描述了通过每周一次的24小时禁食成功减脂的经验，强调这种方法在不感到剥夺的情况下有效。
• josefrichter用简单例子说明，饮食对体重影响更大，单靠运动无法抵消不良饮食带来的影响。
• 71153750指出个体差异和代谢的不同影响，并基于个人跑步经验认为，可以通过大量运动抵消不良饮食的影响。
• regnull分享了通过跟踪饮食和计算卡路里成功控制体重的经验，并推广了自己开发的卡路里跟踪应用。
• JKCalhoun尝试通过小幅调整饮食来减重，但效果不显著，分享了过去通过极端控制饮食成功减重的经历，并对此感到困惑。
• nunez对研究的方法论提出质疑，认为研究未充分考虑热量摄入，且对非洲经济群体的分类和数据处理存在问题，质疑研究的结论是否公正。

补充讨论：
• 研究方法和结论的科学性受到质疑，特别是nunez对研究未考虑热量摄入的批评。
• 个人经验的多样性反映出个体差异对饮食和运动反应的不同，强调了没有单一有效的减重方法。
• 心理策略和生活方式调整在控制体重和健康管理中的重要性被多次提到，如将食品公司视为对手的策略和定期禁食的方法。

Diet, not lack of exercise, drives obesity, a new study finds
One explanation for the rise in obesity in industrialized countries is that people burn fewer calories than people in countries where obesity is rare. A major study finds that's not the case.
You can't outrun a bad diet. Food — not lack of exercise — fuels obesity, study finds
July 24, 2025
5:00 AM ET
Maria Godoy
Diet, not lack of exercise, is driving obesity
Listen
·
3:35
3:35
Toggle more options
Download
Embed
Embed
<
iframe src="https://www.npr.org/player/embed/nx-s1-5477662/nx-s1-9383139" width="100%" height="290" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" title="NPR embedded audio player">
A new study shows people in countries with different obesity rates burn about the same number of calories.
PCH-Vector/iStockphoto via Getty Images
hide caption
toggle caption
PCH-Vector/iStockphoto via Getty Images
Back in the 1800s, obesity was almost nonexistent in the United States. Over the last century, it's become common here and in other industrialized nations, though it remains rare among people who live more traditional lifestyles, such as the
Hadza hunter-gatherers
of Tanzania.
So what's changed? One common explanation is that as societies have developed, they've also become more sedentary, and people have gotten less active. The assumption is that as a result, we burn fewer calories each day, contributing to an energy imbalance that leads to weight gain over time,
says Herman Pontzer,
a professor of evolutionary biology and global health at Duke University who studies how human metabolism has evolved.
Sponsor Message
But in a
major new study
published in the journal
PNAS,
Pontzer and an international team of collaborators found that's not the case. They compared the daily total calorie burn for people from 34 different countries and cultures around the world. The people involved ran the spectrum from hunter-gatherers and farming populations with low obesity rates, to people in more sedentary jobs in places like Europe and the U.S., where obesity is widespread.
"Surprisingly, what we find is that actually, the total calories burned per day is really similar across these populations, even though the lifestyle and the activity levels are really different," says Pontzer.
Shots - Health News
What we know about the health risks of ultra-processed foods
And that finding offers strong evidence that diet — not a lack of physical activity — is the major driver of weight gain and obesity in our modern world.
"This does sort of really fly in the face of what a lot of us anecdotally assumed was driving a lot of the weight gain and obesity today," says
Deirdre Tobias
, an obesity and nutritional epidemiologist at the Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston and the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health. Tobias was not involved in the new research.
Different activity levels, same calorie burn
In the study, researchers examined data for more than 4,200 adult men and women. Study participants were given a special water to drink that contained isotopes that came out in their urine. These isotopes allow scientists to determine exactly how much energy a person expends — not just in active movement, but also the energy it takes to keep our hearts beating, our nervous systems functioning and
just generally stay alive.
Shots - Health News
There's a way to get healthier without even going to a gym. It's called NEAT
"This allows us to get a really accurate measure of how many calories people burn per day over the course of about a week," Pontzer says.
When they adjusted for body size, Pontzer and his colleagues found that people from populations with higher obesity rates burned only slightly less total energy per day than those from populations that weighed less. These differences in energy expenditure didn't contribute much to the differences in obesity rates among populations, he says.
While it may seem implausible that someone who is out foraging for berries all day burns about the same amount of daily calories as, say, your typical office worker, Pontzer says it fits with what scientists have been learning about how our bodies burn calories. Pontzer's past research has suggested that our bodies tend to adjust how we expend energy to keep our total calorie burn stable within a pretty narrow range.
Sponsor Message
"So if we burn more of our energy every day on physical activity, on exercise, after a while our bodies will adjust and spend less energy on the other tasks that we sort of don't notice going on in the background," Pontzer says.
Changing the message on obesity
Shots - Health News
Less snacking, more satisfaction: Some foods boost levels of an Ozempic-like hormone
The new findings have big implications for obesity. If differences in calorie burn can't explain why some countries have higher obesity rates than others, then it must be something else. "And that would be diet," says Tobias, who praised the design of the new study.
"It's 100% the diet," agrees
Dr. Dariush Mo

• com2kid基于个人经验认为，在一定程度上可以通过大量运动抵消不良饮食的影响，但这种方法需要投入的运动量超出了大多数人的意愿。
• ozgrakkurt提出将包装食品公司视为对手的心理策略，帮助自己抵制不健康食品，并强调水果比包装食品更便宜。
• post_break分享了通过控制饮食和步行成功减重40磅的经验，认为不摄入脂肪比通过运动消耗脂肪更有效。
• benabbott推荐通过举重增加肌肉质量，从而提高静息代谢率，认为这是比每天进行有氧运动更有效的长期策略。
• RobKohr描述了通过每周一次的24小时禁食成功减脂的经验，强调这种方法在不感到剥夺的情况下有效。
• josefrichter用简单例子说明，饮食对体重影响更大，单靠运动无法抵消不良饮食带来的影响。
• 71153750指出个体差异和代谢的不同影响，并基于个人跑步经验认为，可以通过大量运动抵消不良饮食的影响。
• regnull分享了通过跟踪饮食和计算卡路里成功控制体重的经验，并推广了自己开发的卡路里跟踪应用。
• JKCalhoun尝试通过小幅调整饮食来减重，但效果不显著，分享了过去通过极端控制饮食成功减重的经历，并对此感到困惑。
• nunez对研究的方法论提出质疑，认为研究未充分考虑热量摄入，且对非洲经济群体的分类和数据处理存在问题，质疑研究的结论是否公正。

补充讨论：
• 研究方法和结论的科学性受到质疑，特别是nunez对研究未考虑热量摄入的批评。
• 个人经验的多样性反映出个体差异对饮食和运动反应的不同，强调了没有单一有效的减重方法。
• 心理策略和生活方式调整在控制体重和健康管理中的重要性被多次提到，如将食品公司视为对手的策略和定期禁食的方法。

data.title: Tram Trains
data.author: ortegaygasset
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了如何在较小城市通过“轨道电车”（tram-train）提供经济有效的公共交通解决方案。许多城市面临铁路线无法贯穿市中心的问题，而通过让火车直接穿越城市可以提高运输效率。大城市如伦敦和巴黎通过建造地下隧道解决了这一问题，但成本高昂。对于较小城市，德国的卡尔斯鲁厄（Karlsruhe）提供了一个成功的 tram-train 模式：将电车与铁路结合，电车不仅在市区运行，还能延伸至郊区。尽管 tram-train 比传统火车慢，因为需要与道路交通共享空间，但它显著提高了运输效率和乘客数量。卡尔斯鲁厄的 tram-train 网络如今每年运送1.7亿人次，长度超过660公里。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同城市中轻轨、有轨电车以及混合交通系统的可行性与优缺点

不同观点：
• kposehn认为，夏洛特的低密度城市结构使得像慕尼黑那样的交通网络不可行。虽然现有的轻轨系统可以连接周围的货运铁路线，但由于美国货运铁路与轻轨系统的碰撞标准不同，联邦铁路管理局（FRA）禁止这两种系统共享同一轨道。不过，可以在足够宽的线路旁新建轨道来实现这一目标。

• xxmarkuski对卡尔斯鲁厄的混合交通系统提出了批评，指出该系统存在严重的质量问题，例如列车容量不足、经常出现延误、不同交通运营者之间的合作不力等。因此，他认为卡尔斯鲁厄的案例不应被盲目视为成功的典范。

• mcv提到了阿姆斯特丹曾经在阿姆斯特尔芬线上同时运行有轨电车和地铁，但因不同站台高度导致长站台问题，最终停止了这种做法。此外，还提到一些城市通过填湖或拆除房屋来为铁路腾出空间的历史。

• PLenz建议重新引入城际铁路（Interurban）作为解决方案，并提供了一个相关的维基百科链接。

• xg15指出科隆的电车系统经过一个世纪的合并与扩展，已经形成了一个独立于国家铁路和市郊火车的网络，与柏林或维也纳的系统有所不同。

• Animats以伦敦为例，指出伦敦的13个主要火车站都是终点站，只有通过昂贵的隧道项目（如横贯铁路）才能实现东西向的贯通服务。

• danhor详细讨论了 tram-train 系统的优缺点，认为其虽然具有灵活性，但在速度和容量上存在不足，尤其不适合北美那些缺乏强中心的城市。此外，提出在美国城市实现 tram-train 系统之前，应该先改善现有的通勤铁路服务和票务整合。

• lmm认为 tram-train 系统被过度炒作，仅在少数城市中表现尚可，并非某些交通爱好者所宣称的万能解决方案。不同城市的需求可能只需要常规的有轨电车、火车或票务整合。

• trollied提到谢菲尔德在英国率先实施了 tram-train 系统，利用国家铁路线运行。

• sschueller介绍了苏黎世的 Forchbahn 系统，该系统在行程中途切换电压，并在城市中转换为地铁运行。

• trgn指出布鲁塞尔的火车在城市中短暂转变为地铁运行，且通常不进行票价检查，提供了一种高频免费南北地铁线的体验。

• fjfaase提供了一个全球 tram-train 系统的维基百科链接供参考。

• jcynix描述了法国梅斯的一种类似有轨电车的公交系统，该系统通过封闭道路运行，连接重要地点，并提供停车换乘服务。

• standardUser提到历史上美国的城际铁路系统曾经非常庞大，并提供了一些现存系统的链接。

• thomasjb建议 tram/tramtrain 系统可以用于货物运输，以减少城市中心的一些轻型货车流量，但认为人力操作可能导致效率低下。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于 tram-train 系统的实际可行性和适用性，特别是在不同城市结构下的表现。例如，卡尔斯鲁厄系统被批评为可靠性差，而一些评论者认为 tram-train 并非所有城市的万能解决方案。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是不同城市如何通过历史或现代手段解决铁路和城市规划的冲突问题，例如阿姆斯特丹和伦敦的案例。
• 票务整合和交通网络的合作运营也被认为是提高系统效率的重要因素。

here
!
Many cities face the following problem. They have railway lines that go where people live. But these railway lines end at the edge of the city center, and don’t go out the other side.
For cities with this problem, the solution is
through running
. Terminating a train and turning it around takes a lot of space, space that is usually unavailable in a city center. This means running a railway line through the city often doubles or triples the number of trains it can handle. As a bonus, passengers who are going from one side of the city to the other can do that much more quickly, with no change.
Many cities, such as London, Paris, Munich and Milan, have used through running to turn some of their existing Victorian railway lines into metro-style services, by building tunnels under the city center. A few other cities, like Berlin, built viaducts (bridges that carry roads and railways over obstacles), while others, such as Cologne, have simply added platforms at their main stations to enable suburban trains to run through. But all of these are big cities, with over a million people, where the property value uplift or extra revenues from fares can cover
the enormous costs
of tunneling. But there is another option, affordable for smaller cities or large towns: the
tram-train
.
A Karlsruhe tram, running on railway tracks. Image credit:
Baden-Wuerttemberg
.
Karlsruhe is a small city of only 300,000 people in southwestern Germany, near the French border. The city’s main station is nearly two kilometers from the city center, following a project in the early twentieth century to build a larger station on a less cramped site. This caused great inconvenience to passengers, who had to change to the city’s tram network in order to get to the old center.
In 1957, the city took the first steps towards creating a new type of transit, the tram-train, when it took over a bankrupt suburban railway, the Albtalbahn, and extended it into the city center over the tram network.
Over the next four years the line’s gauge (the space between the rails) was converted from 1,000 millimeters to 1,435 millimeters, the standard gauge used by the tram network, and it was re-electrified at the same voltage as the tramway. The modernization of the line enabled quicker journey times – the 70 minute journey to Bad Herrenalb, the line’s terminus, was reduced to 46 minutes – but more importantly passengers who wanted to get to the city center did not need to change to a tram.
The idea of a tram that runs outside of a city’s urban area was not new: Vienna, for instance, had been operating a similar line to the neighboring spa town of Baden since 1907. Karlsruhe’s inventive step, which came later, was to extend the tram-train onto railway lines that did not just carry tram traffic. In 1979, the line was extended onto a freight railway north of the city, and in 1992 the first tram-train took over pre-existing passenger services, to the town of Bretten.
Joining the tram and train networks together was
tricky
. German railways are electrified at 15 kilovolts alternating current, while Karlsruhe’s trams use 750 volt direct current, which meant that the city needed to procure trams capable of using both voltages, which were (and still are) rare. The railway and the tram network used two different signaling systems, the ‘traffic lights’ that are used to control the movement of rail traffic. The trams have to use
retractable steps
to overcome the big gap between the 2.65 meter-wide trams and platforms which can handle 3 meter-wide trains. These steps also enable later models of the trams, whose floors are 570 millimeters above the ground, to work with both 380 and 760 millimeter-high platforms.
Overcoming these technical problems led to a much better network.
Ridership of the Bretten line went up 400 percent
after it was extended into the city center on tramlines, and the line now has
18,000 trips per day
, up from 2,000 before the tram-train took over. Passenger numbers on the network
doubled
between 1985 and 1999, after several more lines had been added. The network today, which carries
170 million passengers
per year, is over 660 kilometers long, longer than the combined length of Munich’s tram, metro and suburban railway networks.
Karlruhe’s transit system. Image credit:
Wikimedia Commons.
Tram-trains have trade-offs. Trams are
slower than trains
, because they have to share road space with cars, pedestrians and bicycles. Where possible, therefore, Karls

data.title: Implementing a functional language with graph reduction (2021)
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用Haskell实现一个基于图归约的函数式语言。该实现分为三部分：λ-calculus解析器、λ-calculus到组合逻辑的编译器以及图归约器。首先，通过解析器将λ-calculus和整数解析为简单的表达式。其次，编译器使用括号抽象和优化规则将λ-calculus表达式转换为组合逻辑（S, K, I, B, C, Y）。最后，图归约器将组合逻辑表达式放入图数据结构中，并通过可变的`STRef`引用实现图的原地销毁性归约。本文还展示了如何用Haskell表示λ-表达式和环境，并提供了简单的解析器代码示例。最终，通过SKI组合逻辑的图归约实现了该语言的后端。虽然最初尝试扩展到闭笛卡尔范畴（CCC）失败，但最终成功实现了预期功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于交互网络和图归约计算模型的不同实现和理论联系

不同观点：
• [enricozb] 认为交互网络（interaction nets）是另一种基于图归约的计算模型，并提供了相关思考链接，探讨交互网络与λ演算的关系。
• [tromp] 提到了Ben Lynn在一个IOCCC获奖作品中实现了Haskell的子集，使用图归约引擎进行小型的C程序编译。他还提到Lennart Augustsson实现了更大规模且更适合生产的Haskell到组合子逻辑的编译器，提供了相关资源链接。
• [throwaway81523] 推荐了Simon Peyton Jones（SPJ）关于同一主题的书，暗示该书对理解相关内容非常有帮助，并提供了书籍链接。
• [taliesinb] 从名绑定的角度探讨了图与树之间的关系，并试图寻找单子范畴（monoidal category）相关的形式化理论，特别是将S和K组合子视为类似于复制和删除操作的直觉观察，询问是否存在这种观察的正式版本。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个具体实现和资源链接，如Ben Lynn的编译器实现和Lennart Augustsson的MicroHs项目。
• 争议焦点似乎在于如何形式化地理解组合子逻辑中的操作与范畴论中的概念之间的联系，尤其是对S和K组合子的观察是否存在更正式的理论支持。
• 不同评论者提供了相关的参考资料和文献链接，为深入理解和进一步研究提供了资源。

Implementing a Functional Language with Graph Reduction
Posted on December 27, 2021
by Thomas Mahler
Abstract
Implementing a small functional language with a classic combinator based graph-reduction machine in Haskell.
The implementation is structured into three parts:
A λ-calculus parser from
A Combinatory Compiler
which was extended to cover a tiny functional language based on the untyped λ-calculus.
A compiler from λ-calculus to combinatory logic combinators (S,K,I,B,C and Y) which is based on bracket-abstraction and some optimization rules.
A graph-reducer. Combinator terms are allocated into a graph data-structure.
Which is then reduced by applying combinator graph-reduction. The destructive inplace reduction of the graph is made possible by using
STRef
mutable references.
Introduction
In my
last blog post
I presented two ways of transforming λ-terms into variable free representations:
- bracket abstraction to combinatory logic terms (SKI) and
- bracket abstraction to terms of closed cartesian categories (CCC).
I demonstrated that both representations are equivalent as they imply the same reduction rules.
My original intention was to extend an existing Haskell CCC implementation to a proof-of-concept implementation of a small functional language. I even promised to cover this in my next blog post.
I invested a lot of time in this idea but I failed to get it off the ground.
At least the code of these experiments has been preserved
.
So I came back to writing a SKI graph-reduction as the backend of my language implementation. This is a well-worn path. I took the basic ideas from the classic
compiling functional languages
which dates back to 1988.
Fortunately, I did not fail this time!
In the following I’m explaining my implementation approach. I’ll also share some of my insights and talk about possible future extensions.
representing λ-expressions
I’m aiming at a very rudimentary language that is basically just pure λ-calculus plus integers. Here is an example:

As you can see it’s possible to use classical λ-calculus notation

as well as Haskell syntax:

44685669.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用Haskell实现一个基于图归约的函数式语言。该实现分为三部分：λ-calculus解析器、λ-calculus到组合逻辑的编译器以及图归约器。首先，通过解析器将λ-calculus和整数解析为简单的表达式。其次，编译器使用括号抽象和优化规则将λ-calculus表达式转换为组合逻辑（S, K, I, B, C, Y）。最后，图归约器将组合逻辑表达式放入图数据结构中，并通过可变的`STRef`引用实现图的原地销毁性归约。本文还展示了如何用Haskell表示λ-表达式和环境，并提供了简单的解析器代码示例。最终，通过SKI组合逻辑的图归约实现了该语言的后端。虽然最初尝试扩展到闭笛卡尔范畴（CCC）失败，但最终成功实现了预期功能。

data.title: Never write your own date parsing library
data.author: ulrischa
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了为何不应自行编写日期解析库，并以作者自身的经验为例，讲述了在Eleventy项目中从使用Luxon库到寻找替代方案的过程。最初选择Luxon是因为其准确性和相对较小的体积，但随着项目扩展到更多JavaScript环境，Luxon的体积问题凸显。作者评估了多个替代库，如Moment、Dayjs和Date-fns，发现Dayjs体积小但不够准确。最终，作者决定收紧Eleventy中的默认日期解析规则，并采用RFC 9557作为新的标准，以解决ISO 8601的各种解析问题和不一致性。文章强调了严格解析日期格式的重要性，并指出未来JavaScript的Temporal API将带来更一致的日期处理方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应自行实现日期、时间处理库，以及处理日期和时间相关的复杂性。

不同观点：
• **支持自行实现**：quelsolaar认为，人们应该挑战高难度任务，通过自行实现复杂的功能（如日期库、操作系统等）来学习。高难度任务能提升个人能力，避免只做简单任务。

• **反对自行实现**：davidw和jedberg通过幽默和直白的方式表达，认为自行实现日期库、时间解析等功能通常是不必要的，尤其是考虑到其复杂性。jedberg还扩展到其他如负载均衡、防火墙和电子邮件验证等功能。

• **实际经验分享（支持库使用）**：takinola和jimmaswell强调了使用现有库（如Moment.js）的重要性，以避免处理日期、时区等复杂问题。jimmaswell特别提到Moment虽然进入维护模式，但其稳定性是一个优势，避免了频繁的重大变更。

• **特定场景的自行实现**：aaroninsf分享了在特定场景下自行实现日期解析库的必要性，尤其是处理历史文献中的多样化日期格式。他指出在处理不规范和多语言日期时，需要使用启发式算法和上下文分析。

44685875.article_content:
Never write your own Date Parsing Library
July 23, 2025
Never
write your own date parsing library.
Never
.
No exceptions.
Never have I ever…
So… I’ve written my own date parsing library.
Why?
Our story begins seven years ago in the year 2018. I made the very sensible choice to adopt
luxon
as the Date Parsing library for Eleventy. This parsing behavior is used when Eleventy finds a String for the
date
value in the Data Cascade
(though YAML front matter will bypass this behavior when encountering a YAML-compatible date).
This choice was good for Eleventy’s Node.js-only requirements at the time: accurate and not
too
big (relatively speaking). Eleventy has
used
luxon
since
@0.2.12
and has grown with the dependency all the way through
@3.7.1
. Now that’s what I call a high quality dependency!
As we move Eleventy to run in more JavaScript environments and runtimes (including on the client) we’ve had to take a hard look at our use of Luxon, currently
our
largest
dependency
:
4.7 MB of 21.3 MB (22%) of
@11ty/eleventy
node_modules
229 kB of 806 kB (28%) of
@11ty/client
(
not yet released!
) bundle size (unminified)
Given that our use of Luxon is strictly limited to the
DateTime.fromISO
function for ISO 8601 date parsing
(not formatting or display), it would have been nice to enable tree-shaking on the Luxon library to reduce its size in the bundle (though that wouldn’t have helped the
node_modules
size, I might have settled for that trade-off). Unfortunately,
Luxon does not yet support tree-shaking
so it’s an all or nothing for the bundle.
The Search Begins
I did the next sensible thing and looked at a few alternatives:
Package
Type
Disk Size
Bundle Size
luxon
@3.7.1
Dual
4.59 MB
81.6 kB
(min)
moment
@2.30.1
CJS
4.35 MB
294.9 kB
(min)
dayjs
@1.11.13
CJS
670 kB
6.9 kB
(min)
date-fns
@4.1.0
Dual
22.6 MB
77.2 kB
(min)
The next in line to the throne was clearly
dayjs
, which is small on disk and in bundle size. Unfortunately I found it to be inaccurate:
dayjs
fails about 80 of the 228 tests in the test suite I’m using moving forward.
As an aside, this search has made me tempted to ask: do we need to keep Dual publishing packages? I prefer ESM over CJS but maybe just pick one?
Breaking Changes
Most date parsing woes (in my opinion) come from ambiguity: from supporting
too many
formats or attempting maximum flexibility in parsing. And guess what: ISO 8601 is a big ’ol standard with a lot of subformats. There is a maintenance freedom and simplicity in strict parsing requirements (don’t let XHTML hear me say that).
Consider
"200"
. Is this the year 200? Is this the 200th day of the current year? Surprise, in ISO 8601 it’s neither — it’s
a decade, spanning from the year 2000 to the year 2010
. And
"20"
is the century from the year 2000 to the year 2100.
Moving forward, we’re tightening up the default date parsing in Eleventy (this is
configurable
— keep using Luxon if you want!).
Luckily we have a north star date format:
RFC 9557
, billed as
“an extension to the ISO 8601 / RFC 3339”
formats and already in use by the upcoming Temporal web standard APIs for date and time parsing coming to a JavaScript runtime near you.

data.title: The sad state of font rendering on Linux (2018)
data.author: harporoeder
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Linux字体渲染的不足，作者以Windows的ClearType渲染为基准，认为其更利于阅读。文章解释了字体渲染的基本概念，如矢量数据的光栅化、子像素渲染、子像素定位、字体微调和抗锯齿。不同操作系统在字体渲染上采取不同策略，Windows集成了所有先进技术，尤其在Windows 7中达到了锐利的字体效果，但也有色彩边缘问题。Windows 8及之后版本则回归灰度平滑，字体较模糊。

关于macOS，作者最初批评其渲染过于模糊和粗体，但在收到反馈后，验证了High Sierra版本之前的macOS使用子像素抗锯齿，效果较好。作者推测，由于微软ClearType技术的专利限制，苹果可能避免使用相关技术，导致其渲染在锐利度上不如Windows理想。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：操作系统中的字体渲染质量，特别是子像素渲染（subpixel rendering）的效果及其实现差异

不同观点：
• jchw：认为Microsoft早期的子像素渲染做得不好，但DirectWrite有所改进。同时提到Linux上的情况较差，并分享了关于伽马校正的额外阅读材料。
• zekica：反驳说Linux上的子像素渲染是正常的，自己正在使用KDE和Firefox的子像素渲染，且效果良好。
• neoden：指出引用的文章是2018年的，认为应在标题中注明时间。
• scblock：强烈批评Windows的字体渲染，认为其在现代操作系统中最差，尤其在QD-OLED屏幕上会出现颜色边缘效应。同时认为Linux和Mac OS的渲染效果远胜于Windows。
• ranger207：认为Linux的字体渲染不错，但MacOS的渲染最差，并认为字体渲染是主观感受，因人而异。
• omnimus：指出字体本身带有渲染提示表，许多开源字体由于缺乏资源或能力，渲染质量不如Apple或Microsoft的字体。
• necovek：怀念以前在Freetype中可以轻松调整渲染强度和RGB布局的设置，认为MacOS今天很糟糕，但仍比Windows好。
• bradfitz：认为在超过215ppi的显示器上，这些关于子像素渲染的讨论已经过时。
• ndiddy：解释了Linux上安装的微软核心字体为何质量差，因为这些字体自2000年以来未更新。
• RGBCube：分享了一个Freetype的设置，可以实现接近MacOS质量的字体渲染，但仅适用于高DPI显示器。
• zzo38computer：偏好使用非Unicode的位图字体，但在Linux上许多程序不支持。
• omnimus（补充）：字体渲染非常主观，人们往往偏好自己习惯的渲染方式。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到Linux字体渲染的质量问题，并引用了其他关于Linux字体渲染的讨论链接。
• 有人质疑文章中对Freetype图片的批评，认为文章未清晰说明问题所在。

争议焦点：
• Windows、Linux和MacOS之间的字体渲染质量对比，特别是子像素渲染的效果。
• 字体渲染是否主观，是否因个人习惯和使用经验而异。

总结：
评论围绕不同操作系统中的字体渲染质量展开，特别是子像素渲染的效果。参与者对Windows、Linux和MacOS的渲染效果各持己见，有些人认为渲染效果非常主观，因人而异。另外，开源字体与商业字体的质量差异也被提及。

The sad state of font rendering on Linux | Infosec scribbles
Blog
Fonts Stuff
My Public Projects
About Author
December 21, 2018, updated on August 10, 2019
The sad state of font rendering on Linux
Preamble
As it turns out, font rendering is a highly controversial topic. If you don’t see anything wrong with Linux font rendering, please disregard this as a shitpost. Thanks.
I spent the first 25 years of my life on Windows and therefore I am biased towards Windows font rendering with ClearType. I also agree with
research which suggests that
this rendering approach
makes reading easier on the eyes
. There are also some facts you can’t argue with, such as non-linear rendering without anti-aliasing looking awful.
With that out of the way, let’s proceed.
Basic concepts
Fonts are vector data that gets rasterized when displayed to the user. Computer displays are low-DPI devices for complex reasons, and such DPI (96) is not enough to display fonts without a myriad of trade-offs. Most notable are sub-pixel rendering, sub-pixel positioning, font hinting and anti-aliasing. You can read up more
here
and
here
if you want the full background.
Each operating system approaches font rendering differently. To get Windows-like rendering that I prefer, anti-aliasing, sub-pixel rendering, sub-pixel positioning and font hinting based on byte code embedded into fonts - basically, every step of the technological progress made in the last 30 years - need to be active.
Windows implementation
Simply put, Windows uses every font rendering improvement technology available
and
goes a step further to use fonts specifically designed to look great when combined with this technology. It is state of the art and then some.
One obvious thing you can see on the zoomed in part of the image is that black and white text is not actually black and white on Windows 7. Since sub-pixel rendering relies on toggling red, green and blue parts of a single pixel, it introduces
colour fringing
. A small percentage of people can see so well, that they actually notice this when reading. They can disable this feature at the cost of less sharp fonts or migrate to Windows 8 or newer.
Windows font rendering keeps changing with every new version of the OS. Windows 7 had the sharpest fonts, while from Windows 8 onwards Microsoft went back to grayscale font smoothing, resulting in blurrier fonts without colour fringing. This is how FreeType code in
/include/freetype/ftdriver.h
documents Windows font rendering evolution over time:

I don’t see colour fringing, so my preference is 39/DWrite/v2.0 rendering of Windows 7.
OS X implementation
OS X
has the absolute worst font rendering from the readability aspect. It does not use hinting at all and relies only on grayscale anti-aliasing. This combination makes everything appear very bold and blurry:
There is not even a hint of any consistency in the rendering either, thickness is all over the place even within a single glyph, with different strokes “sticking” together because of the lack of pixels:
This distracts your subconsciousness and wastes attention on just recognizing glyphs and their edges, resulting in massive eye strain. Don’t believe me? Do a controlled reading speed experiment against Windows.
When this blog post got featured on Reddit and HackerNews, a number of people pointed out that prior to Mojave, which was the latest release at the time the post was written, OS X used to have sub-pixel anti-aliasing, text rendering was great, I was wrong and Apple did not deserve the hate. To verify this, I temporarily got my hands on a box running High Sierra and did some comparisons.
As you can see here, indeed, OS X had sub-pixel anti-aliasing in High Sierra, which provided less boldness and bluriness with somewhat better consistency in glyph thickness. However, colour fringing on High Sierra is rather apparent. Rendering is still rather blurry, closer to the FreeType auto-hinter than to what
I
would consider an optimal result.
I have not reverse-engineered Apple’s font rendering code, but this would explain what I am seeing:
Microsoft patented ClearType rendering and Apple took care not to step on their toes
Sub-pixel rendering techniques patented in ClearType may have a better trade-off between colour fringing and sharpness than those used in Apple’s Quartz

44685587.article_summary:
本文讨论了Linux字体渲染的不足，作者以Windows的ClearType渲染为基准，认为其更利于阅读。文章解释了字体渲染的基本概念，如矢量数据的光栅化、子像素渲染、子像素定位、字体微调和抗锯齿。不同操作系统在字体渲染上采取不同策略，Windows集成了所有先进技术，尤其在Windows 7中达到了锐利的字体效果，但也有色彩边缘问题。Windows 8及之后版本则回归灰度平滑，字体较模糊。

关于macOS，作者最初批评其渲染过于模糊和粗体，但在收到反馈后，验证了High Sierra版本之前的macOS使用子像素抗锯齿，效果较好。作者推测，由于微软ClearType技术的专利限制，苹果可能避免使用相关技术，导致其渲染在锐利度上不如Windows理想。
44685587.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：操作系统中的字体渲染质量，特别是子像素渲染（subpixel rendering）的效果及其实现差异

不同观点：
• jchw：认为Microsoft早期的子像素渲染做得不好，但DirectWrite有所改进。同时提到Linux上的情况较差，并分享了关于伽马校正的额外阅读材料。
• zekica：反驳说Linux上的子像素渲染是正常的，自己正在使用KDE和Firefox的子像素渲染，且效果良好。
• neoden：指出引用的文章是2018年的，认为应在标题中注明时间。
• scblock：强烈批评Windows的字体渲染，认为其在现代操作系统中最差，尤其在QD-OLED屏幕上会出现颜色边缘效应。同时认为Linux和Mac OS的渲染效果远胜于Windows。
• ranger207：认为Linux的字体渲染不错，但MacOS的渲染最差，并认为字体渲染是主观感受，因人而异。
• omnimus：指出字体本身带有渲染提示表，许多开源字体由于缺乏资源或能力，渲染质量不如Apple或Microsoft的字体。
• necovek：怀念以前在Freetype中可以轻松调整渲染强度和RGB布局的设置，认为MacOS今天很糟糕，但仍比Windows好。
• bradfitz：认为在超过215ppi的显示器上，这些关于子像素渲染的讨论已经过时。
• ndiddy：解释了Linux上安装的微软核心字体为何质量差，因为这些字体自2000年以来未更新。
• RGBCube：分享了一个Freetype的设置，可以实现接近MacOS质量的字体渲染，但仅适用于高DPI显示器。
• zzo38computer：偏好使用非Unicode的位图字体，但在Linux上许多程序不支持。
• omnimus（补充）：字体渲染非常主观，人们往往偏好自己习惯的渲染方式。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到Linux字体渲染的质量问题，并引用了其他关于Linux字体渲染的讨论链接。
• 有人质疑文章中对Freetype图片的批评，认为文章未清晰说明问题所在。

争议焦点：
• Windows、Linux和MacOS之间的字体渲染质量对比，特别是子像素渲染的效果。
• 字体渲染是否主观，是否因个人习惯和使用经验而异。

总结：
评论围绕不同操作系统中的字体渲染质量展开，特别是子像素渲染的效果。参与者对Windows、Linux和MacOS的渲染效果各持己见，有些人认为渲染效果非常主观，因人而异。另外，开源字体与商业字体的质量差异也被提及。

data.title: How to configure X11 in a simple way
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何在使用X服务器而非Wayland的FreeBSD系统上，通过简单、成熟的老式工具和程序实现各种桌面环境效果，避免现代Linux桌面环境中常见的臃肿问题。文章涵盖了多个设置主题，包括：

1. **高分屏设置**：通过修改`xorg.conf`文件，根据显示器实际尺寸调整DPI，使GUI元素大小适中，避免眼部疲劳。
2. **键盘配置**：使用shell和文本编辑器完成。
3. **指向设备设置**：包括为左撇子用户配置轨迹球。
4. **屏幕保护程序**：使用经典的XScreenSaver。
5. **效果设置**：如透明度、阴影和动画，适用于轻量级窗口管理器如StumpWM。
6. **多显示器配置**：使用`xrandr`切换显示设置。
7. **显示管理器**：使用依赖较少的XDM。
8. **文件管理器和邮件客户端设置**：如使用Emacs Dired作为默认文件管理器。
9. **主题设置**：通过编辑文本文件实现，无需GUI工具。

文章强调通过成熟工具和方法实现功能，而不依赖大型桌面环境的框架和库。

Preamble
The modern common Linux and as a result also a UNIX desktop is
heavily
bloated
. Even if you install not a full-scale DE like Gnome, but a
small WM: i3wm, WindowMaker, XFCE, StumpWM, etc. These window managers
are small itself, but when user installs a necessary GUI programs —
then a lot of
bloat
will be installed too: gsettings-daemon, D-Bus
daemon, polkitd, console-kit-daemon, etc, etc…
What can I do with all these
bloatware
? There are two solutions:
Disable unwanted compile-time options and recompile necessary stuff
by itself. I already wrote something about this approach
here
.
There is one disadvantage — sometimes you need to edit the source
code or port-related files to get rid of strange things, like
Krita's Wayland dependency when I'm using it in the pure X11
environment and so on.
Use good, old and mature, well-tested by time programs and
solutions. You don't obliged to install a lot of Gnome/KDE-related
libraries if you want a simple program with GUI to achieve a simple
task, like draw a login window and check user's credentials for the
single-user box.
In this post I'll write about the second approach — how to make nice
things with simple (for the "modern" world; of course some purist will
say that even
these
things are bloated too) good old programs and
ways.
All nice things from desktop environments, like nice effects, nice
themes, automatic execution of mail client after click on the proper
link, etc — don't need tons of frameworks and libraries from big
desktop environments. They are totally acessible with an elegant
utilities from a more civilized era.
Actions, described in this blogpost, were (obviously) performed in the
FreeBSD 14.3, not in Linux :-) and with X server, not Wayland :-).
Covered topics:
How to setup X server to operate with HighDPI display?
How to setup keyboard only with a shell and text editor?
How to setup different pointing devices, including tricky setup of
trackball for left-handed user?
Good old XScreenSaver.
How to setup nice effects: transparency, shadows and animations —
for a small WM (e.g. StumpWM)?
How to switch multi-monitor configurations and perform tricky things
with
xrandr
?
How to use XDM as a display manager and login screen? It has a very
limited set of dependencies, lesser than a "lightweight" LightDM.
How to use xdg-utils to open Emacs Dired as a default filemanager,
Emacs ComposeMode as a default e-mail composer, etc?
How to setup some nice themes without GUI utilities — just by
editing text files with any text editor?
High DPI
I have a small 13.3" display with a 2K resolultion in my laptop. As a
result, by default I see all GUI element on my screen very small, so I
can't see them without unnecessary strain in my eyes (and not only I,
of course).
The usual approach to this problem — instruct GUI environment that
this screen with a big resolution doesn't have a big diagonal too.
So, I read these articles:
HiDPI
in the ArchWiki
HOWTO set DPI in Xorg
And also a
man 5 xorg.conf
. Suddenly I found that I don't need to play
with tricky environment variables to please every GUI toolkit. All
that I need to do — is to specify active area dimensions in
millimeters for my monitor in X11 configuration! The neat part — this
settings will be applied to the whole system (login window, any WM,
etc), not only for logged in user with necessary environment
variables.
I got the necessary dimensions in millimeters from a display module
datasheet:
Active area dimensions (mm) from Sharp LQ125T1JW02 datasheet
And specified these dimensions in the proper section (file
/usr/local/etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/10-intel.conf
):
Section "Monitor"
Identifier  "MainMonitor"
Option      "Primary" "true"
DisplaySize 276.48 155.52
EndSection
The
MainMonitor
is specified in the
Device
section as monitor
connected to the DP-3 bus:
Section "Device"
Identifier  "intel"
...
Option      "Monitor-DP-3"   "MainMonitor"
Option      "Monitor-LVDS-1" "PhantomMonitor"
EndSection
And both sections are connected in the
Screen
section:
Section "Screen"
Identifier "MainScreen"
Device     "intel"
Monitor    "MainMonitor"
EndSection

data.title: Efficient Computer's Electron E1 CPU – 100x more efficient than Arm?
data.author: rpiguy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一种新型CGRA架构的效率、应用场景和潜在问题

不同观点：
• [pclmulqdq] 认为该架构类似于FPGA，但单元更大，效率在代码适合单一阵列时非常高，但当代码超出特定规模时，网格配置切换会消耗大量时间和功耗。
• [gamache] 指出该架构与GreenArray GA144相似，但担忧缺乏独特的FORTH方言可能影响市场接受度。
• [pedalpete] 质疑CPU是否真的是嵌入式设计中的能耗瓶颈，指出其他组件如扬声器和屏幕可能更耗电。
• [nnx] 认为该架构可能适合LLM推理，但疑惑为何未在这方面进行市场推广。
• [ACCount36] 认为该架构无法取代通用目的的Arm核心，但在低功耗优化和实时控制核心中可能有应用价值。
• [ZiiS] 对该架构在通用计算上比ARM更高效的可能性表示怀疑。
• [Grosvenor] 将其比作Itanium，指出静态调度和编译器优化的挑战。
• [archipelago123] 解释这是一种数据流架构，指出难以利用数据局部性，且现代乱序核心已解决了一些该架构试图解决的问题。
• [rpiguy] 比较该架构与Apple的神经引擎设计，质疑其在标量任务和多分支情况下的表现。
• [variadix] 对效率提升持保留态度，担心程序超出网格时的表现，并指出需要“足够聪明的编译器”，可能面临与FPGA类似的综合时间问题。

补充讨论：
• [Imustaskforhelp] 请求简化的解释。
• [kendalf89] 联想到编程游戏TIS-100。
• [icandoit] 提到与交互组合子的相似性，并讨论翻译层的构建。
• [vendiddy] 询问该架构是否类似于每个芯片上有多个小处理器。
• [wolfi1] 将其比作transputer架构的单硅片实现。

争议焦点：
• 该架构的实际能效和应用场景，尤其是在通用计算和特定领域（如LLM推理）中的潜力。
• 编译器优化和程序超出网格时的性能问题。

data.title: Monotonic and wall clock time in the Go time package
data.author: valyala
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要介绍了Go语言中`time`包对两种时钟——挂钟（wall clock）和单调时钟（monotonic clock）的处理方式。挂钟显示实际时间，可能会因同步或手动调整而前后跳动，而单调时钟则只会稳定向前，不会回退，适用于测量时间间隔。

在Go 1.9之前，`time.Now()`仅使用挂钟时间，这可能导致时钟调整引发的错误。自Go 1.9起，`time.Now()`返回的`time.Time`结构包含挂钟时间和可选的单调时钟读数。单调时钟读数仅在调用`time.Now()`时设置，其他构造方法如`time.Date`、`time.Unix`、`time.Parse`等不会设置它。

文章还指出，直接比较`time.Time`值可能导致错误，因为像`now.UTC()`和`now.Truncate(0)`这样的方法会移除单调时钟部分，导致比较结果不一致。

总之，文章强调了在处理时间时，理解这两种时钟的区别以及正确使用`time.Now()`的重要性。

by
Phuong Le

Monotonic and Wall Clock Time in the Go time package
Modern operating systems usually keep track of two kinds of clocks: a wall clock and a monotonic clock.
The wall clock is the “real-world” clock that shows calendar dates and times, like UTC or your local time. This clock can be adjusted for synchronization (for example, using NTP) or manually changed by system administrators. It can also suddenly jump due to daylight saving time or leap seconds.
Note
NTP (Network Time Protocol) is a standard internet protocol that allows computers to exchange timestamps. Computers use NTP to synchronize their clocks to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Over the public internet, NTP usually achieves accuracy within a few milliseconds, and on fast local networks, it can be accurate to less than one millisecond.
Since wall clocks can jump forward or backward, slow down, or speed up, measuring time intervals directly using the wall clock can cause errors. For example, syncing time using NTP might slightly speed up or slow down the clock, or inserting a leap second can cause the same second to repeat, etc.
Before Go version 1.9, the time API only used wall-clock time. This created bugs when the clock was adjusted. A famous example was a leap-second bug that caused a
Cloudflare outage in 2016
.
To fix these issues, operating systems also use a second type of clock: a monotonic clock. This clock never goes backward. It only moves forward steadily and cannot be manually adjusted.
Because each clock behaves differently, they have separate purposes:
Wall clocks are for “telling time” (giving timestamps that have meaning globally).
Monotonic clocks are for reliably “measuring time intervals.”
Go follows this same approach.
Monotonic Clock
#
In Go, when you call
time.Now()
, the function returns a
time.Time
struct representing the current moment. This struct actually holds two different values: the wall clock time and an (optional) monotonic clock reading.
The monotonic part is stored internally in the
ext
field of the
time.Time
struct. You can’t access this directly through Go’s public API â it’s only used behind the scenes.
Since the monotonic reading is tied specifically to your current process and system uptime, it has no real meaning outside your running program. That’s why, when you serialize a
time.Time
, the monotonic component isn’t included.
But you may notice during debugging that printing a
time.Time
struct gives you an extra suffix like
m=+0.000123456
:
func
main
()
{
now
:=
time
.
Now
()
fmt
.
Println
(
now
)
// 2024-11-10 23:00:00 +0000 UTC m=+0.001219709
}
That
m=
value shows the monotonic clock offset (in seconds) at the exact moment your
time.Time
was captured. In the example above, this means
0.001219709
seconds passed since the program started running.
When your Go program starts, it notes the current operating system’s monotonic clock value. Each time you call
time.Now()
, Go calculates how much time has passed since your program began. This is what the hidden monotonic field shows: elapsed nanoseconds since your process started, not since your machine booted.
Common Mistakes
#
The monotonic clock in
time.Time
is optional. A
time.Time
value only includes a monotonic reading when it is created directly by the runtime.
This happens in exactly one place: when you call
time.Now()
. Other ways to construct a
time.Time
value, such as
time.Date
,
time.Unix
,
time.Parse
, or any unmarshaling function, never set the monotonic flag.
These only set the wall-clock time:
func
main
()
{
now
:=
time
.
Now
()
fmt
.
Println
(
now
)
fmt
.
Println
(
now
.
UTC
())
fmt
.
Println
(
now
.
Truncate
(
0
))
fmt
.
Println
(
time
.
Date
(
2025
,
7
,
13
,
0
,
0
,
0
,
0
,
time
.
UTC
))
}
// Output:
// 2025-07-13 12:14:36.707899 +0000 UTC m=+0.000080168
// 2025-07-13 12:14:36.707899 +0000 UTC
// 2025-07-13 12:14:36.707899 +0000 UTC
// 2025-07-13 00:00:00 +0000 UTC
You can see that the last three timers do not have the
m=
prefix.
Note
The example above assumes your location uses the UTC timezone. To get the same output, set your system timezone to UTC if needed:
func
init
()
{
os
.
Setenv
(
"TZ"
,
"UTC"
)
}
Comparing Two time.Time Values
#
A common mistake is comparing
time.Time
values using the equality operator:
func
main
()
{
now
:=
time
.
Now
()
nowUTC
:=
now
.
UTC
()
nowTruncated
:=
now
.
Truncate
(
0
)
fmt
.
Println
(
now
==
nowUTC
)
// false
fmt
.
Println
(
now
==
nowTruncated
)
// false
fmt
.
Println
(
nowUTC
==
nowTruncated
)
// false
}
There are two problems with this. First, when you call
now.UTC()
or
now.Truncate(0)
, these methods deliberately remove the monotonic part from the original value. That’s why
now != nowTruncated
.

now.UTC()

data.title: CO2 Battery
data.author: xnx
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种用于长时储能的CO2电池技术。该技术通过封闭的热机械转化过程，利用CO2在气液态之间的转换来发电，具有高效（往返效率75%以上）、成本效益高（具备竞争力的资本和运营支出）、灵活（可在全球任何地方建造）、耐用（30年以上无容量或性能衰减）、可靠（使用环保材料的现成组件）以及独立（不依赖锂等稀有金属）等优点。该技术已在兆瓦级工厂中得到验证并与电网连接。文中还提到Energy Dome公司的解决方案，通过从储气罐中抽取CO2并加压储存，然后通过涡轮机发电，实现长时储能。该技术被视为传统能源存储方案的替代选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新型长时储能技术（如基于二氧化碳的机械储能）的可行性、成本效益、技术细节及其与锂电池和压缩空气储能（CAES）等技术的比较。

不同观点：
• **成本与市场竞争**：
   - conradev指出，锂离子电池成本迅速下降，新技术的市场竞争风险大，尤其是需要大规模投资的情况下。同时，引用了Form Energy等公司面临的挑战。
   - epistasis强调，新的储能技术必须在某些指标上优于锂电池，尤其是成本效益（$/kWh）和循环效率等方面，才能在市场上立足。

• **是否为长时储能**：
   - credit_guy质疑该技术自称的“长时储能”标签，认为仅能存储8小时的能量并不能满足长时储能的需求，且若要具有经济性，长时储能应比短时储能便宜得多。
   - epistasis也指出，长时储能技术需要考虑充放电频率和能量泄漏等因素，以评估其经济潜力。

• **技术细节与数据透明度**：
   - gs17批评该技术的宣传材料缺乏具体数据，仅提供了一些模糊的参数，无法让潜在用户全面了解技术性能。
   - calmbonsai提出了一系列关键问题，包括能量密度、CapEx计算方法、充放电速率以及系统扩展能力等。

• **热力学与效率问题**：
   - nine_k从热力学角度质疑该技术的效率，尤其是气体膨胀时的吸热过程、压缩时的放热处理以及整体循环效率如何达到75%。
   - Peteragain同样对75%的循环效率表示怀疑，认为压缩机和涡轮机的效率组合难以达到如此高的水平。

• **环境与安全问题**：
   - darksaints担心大量二氧化碳集中存储可能带来的安全隐患，提到了历史上与二氧化碳相关的自然灾害。

• **与其他技术的比较**：
   - benlivengood提到该技术在高温差环境下可能带来的附加效益，如结合空调系统提升整体能效。
   - bee_rider和ricciardo则将该技术与压缩空气储能（CAES）进行比较，质疑其相对于锂电池和CAES的实际优势和缺点。

补充讨论：
• **市场潜力和技术多样性**：
   - datadrivenangel认为该技术具有潜力，因为它增加了储能技术的选择多样性，并可能降低对特定矿物的依赖，特别是在与太阳能结合使用时。

争议焦点：
• 该技术是否真正具备长时储能的经济性和效率，尤其是在与锂电池的竞争中。
• 技术细节不透明，导致外界对其性能和安全性的质疑。
• 热力学效率和安全性的争议，特别是二氧化碳的存储和使用是否会带来环境风险。
